brewing.notes: A safe starting point for raw pu-erh: rinse once, gongfu style, short early steeps.

description:
An old-tree raw pu-erh from Ma'anshan Village, Mangbing Township, in Zhenkang County, Lincang. The same name also belongs to the mountain east of the Nanmeng River in Mengku, Shuangjiang County, known there as the Eastern Half Mountain.

Treat it as you would any raw pu-erh: rinse the leaf, keep early steeps short, and ask which year and which trees it comes from, since village names on Yunnan teas are often stretched.
history: The Zhenkang old-tree garden is put at 1,452 meters, with humid air and particular soils credited for its character. It is counted among Lincang's noted teas, and little more is documented about its past.
processing: Typical of raw pu-erh: sun-dried large-leaf mao cha, usually steamed and stone-pressed, then left to age slowly.
harvest_season: Usually spring leaf is prized, as with most raw pu-erh.
appearance_dry: Large, handsome buds with little down; the dry leaf is mostly a dark ink green.
taste_profile: Fresh and full, with light bitterness and astringency, a high lasting aroma and a sweet return.
vintage_note: Raw pu-erh is sold by harvest year: young at 1 to 3 years, mid-aged at 5 to 10, aged at 15 or more. Storage matters as much as age.
